gen-mystery-quest-gf-farro: Farro draws every stroke at a single thickness with short ascenders, so its lines look tidy and friendly on the page. Mystery Quest's bookish heading then feels like a bigger voice nearby.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lays its letters out like nails on a ruler, one stroke width through the whole alphabet. Mystery Quest does the nostalgic, bookish flourish with open curves, while Fragment Mono keeps the structure precise.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-geist-mono: Structured and technical, Geist Mono sets fixed-width letters with big side gaps and lowercase that rises high, all outlined at one steady thickness. Under Mystery Quest, it feels measured.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-genos: Tight, modern, a bit crisp. Mystery Quest brings its open-jawed, nostalgic curves to the top, and Genos follows with a high midline and moderate thick-thin modulation that keeps the text moving without snagging.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-geom: Mystery Quest opens with bookish, nostalgic curves and compact ascenders sitting over its tall lowercase letters, each stroke wide at the jaw. Geom adds a lofty, approachable lowercase band underneath, so the page moves from storybook to contemporary.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-hammersmith-one: Hammersmith One keeps capitals barely taller than lowercase, with rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord. Hammersmith One has no quill-style tapering, so text reads smooth and clean beside the bookish curves of Mystery Quest.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-inder: Professional and clean, Inder shows little height difference between its capitals and lowercase. And Mystery Quest, with open jaws on every curve, gives the pair its real strength: a nostalgic heading over a sturdy, level body.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-jaldi: Mystery Quest brings bookish, nostalgic curves with compact ascenders, while Jaldi packs brushed letters tightly under it with an x-height pushed well above the usual. The pairing's best quality is that approachable, professional body supporting a storybook heading.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Open jaws on every curved stroke give Mystery Quest its bookish, nostalgic look. Kdam Thmor Pro fills the line with its bowls, so a heading shrunk down would lose ground to the modern body.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-krona-one: Mystery Quest lends bookish, nostalgic curves and compact ascenders, while Krona One spaces its letters loosely with a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. Heading and body feel like an old storybook with a plain sans partner.
